hook_text: A rectangle has 4 lines of symmetry. True or false? Fold it and see.
clip_script: Soweto, a class getting ready for Youth Day. Fold paper, cut, open: a heart, and the fold line is a line of symmetry. The two halves match exactly. A square has 4 lines: up, across and both diagonals. A rectangle? Fold along the diagonal and the corners stick out. Only 2 lines. A triangle with equal sides has 3. A circle has more than you can draw. The letter S looks balanced but has none. On grid paper, each corner gets a partner the same number of squares away.
visual_style: Paper folding open into a heart, then a rectangle folding along its diagonal with flaps sticking out.
mood: Proud and creative, like getting a display ready for a school event.
pacing: Fold and reveal, then count lines, then the rectangle trap and the letter S.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the lines of symmetry in your own name.
